item.title: Military ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍⁠‌​‌‌‍⁠‌​kills 21 ISWAP fighters
item.description: …forces 26 terrorists, family members to surrender The Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) have intensified offensives against terrorist networks, killing 21 ISWAP fighters, including senior commanders, and recording the surrender of 26 fighters and their family members in the Northeast. The Director, Defence Media Operations, Maj.-Gen. Michael Onoja, disclosed this in a statement on ongoing military operations covering Nov. 13 to Nov. 19. Onoja said precision air strikes conducted between Monday and Tuesday around Monguno and Arinna in the South Lake Chad area of Borno neutralised 21 ISWAP fighters and severely injured 10 others. He said the first strike killed seven terrorists, including members of the group’s Improvised Explosive Device (IED) network, and incapacitated a key IED expert. According to him, the second engagement at Arinna neutralised a member of ISWAP’s Shura Council, who served as its Provost Commander, a Qaid of Sabon Tumbu and 12 other fighters. The director said the sustained military pressure also prompted 26 terrorists and their family members, comprising eight fighters and 18 family members, to surrender between Nov. 13 and Nov. 18. He said the surrender took place in Bama, Dikwa, Gwoza, Kukawa and Monguno Local Government Areas of Borno. Among those who surrendered were 12 women and children who fled Bula Daloye on Nov. 13, as well as a terrorist who surrendered along Gwoza-Pulka Road on Nov. 14. “The latter reportedly handed over an AK-47 rifle, five magazines, 34 rounds of ammunition and two hand grenades,” he said. Onoja said the surrendering terrorists cited intense military operations and internal clashes between rival factions as reasons for abandoning the group. He added that troops also rescued four internally displaced persons who escaped from terrorist captivity at Zaha Village in the Mandara Mountains, Gwoza LGA, on Tuesday. Onoja further disclosed that troops arrested suspected terrorist collaborators and logistics suppliers in Borno, Yobe and Kano, including individuals allegedly conveying combat materials and supplies to terrorist enclaves. In the Northwest, he said the troops of Operation Fansan Yamma rescued three kidnapped victims along Anka-Gada Mayya Road in Zamfara on Nov. 12 and captured a vehicle belonging to the terrorists. According to him, troops also neutralised one terrorist during an engagement at Aguba Village in Kajuru LGA of Kaduna on Nov. 14, recovering two fabricated rifles and a mobile phone. Onoja said troops arrested a principal suspect in Ribah, whose confession reportedly led to the arrest of three other persons linked to an illegal supply network serving bandits along the Bena axis. “In the North-Central, troops of Operation Enduring Peace recovered a PKT machine gun, three AK-47 rifles and three magazines surrendered by fleeing terrorists following sustained offensives around Odare Forest in Kanam LGA of Plateau. “Troops of Operation Whirl Stroke also arrested suspected arms and logistics

item.title: Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list
item.description: Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured the leader of a drug-trafficking group who was among the 10 most-wanted fugitives sought by US law enforcement. Fausto Isidro Meza, alias “Chapo Isidro,” and two other leaders of his drug gang were captured during a special forces raid Friday night in Sinaloa state, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat announced on X. A firefight ensued between the military and gang members in the town of Guasave, sparking panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game, local media reported. “Chapo Isidro” is the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico’s military said. He was captured alongside his number two in the group and another man identified as a financial operator. They were all transported by a Mexican Air Force aircraft to Mexico City “to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities,” the military said. Chapo Isidro faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States. The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. Giving his name as Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, the FBI bulletin says his group is responsible for importing “large quantities of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl, and marijuana into the United States.” The post Mexico captures drug kingpin on FBI’s most wanted list appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FG increases medical student admission to 12,000, targets 20,000 annually — Alausa
item.description: The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has said. Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan (UI), on Saturday, said that it targets enrollment of 20,000 students annually. The minister said the increase in enrollment was part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector amid the migration of Nigerian medical professionals abroad. He said that the government, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, had increased nursing enrollment from about 28,000 annually to more than 130,000. According to him, the country is making progress in producing more healthcare professionals. Alausa, who represented Tinubu at the inauguration, said the administration was investing in infrastructure to expand the capacity of medical schools and other tertiary institutions to accommodate more students. According to him, annual admission into medical schools has risen to about 12,000, from 5,000 students recorded before the administration began in May 2023. “We decided that in four years, we will increase the number to 20,000 annually. “Three years into it, we are enrolling about 12,000 medical students now across all our medical schools in the country, and by the end of 2028, we will meet our target of enrolling over 20,000 medical students,” he said. Alausa said the government had also increased admission into dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and other allied health programs to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce. He said the expansion was being complemented by investments in infrastructure, including hostels, to support increased enrollment and improve the learning environment. The minister added that the government was also investing in the education sector through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative. “This includes the construction and rehabilitation of schools, expansion of medical schools, and re-equipping of engineering workshops,” the minister said. Alausa said the administration had invested nearly N500 billion in educational infrastructure, adding that the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had also expanded access to tertiary education for students irrespective of their economic backgrounds. He urged journalists to verify the figures on nursing and medical student enrollment through the relevant regulatory bodies, including the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. (NAN) The post FG increases medical student admission to 12,000, targets 20,000 annually — Alausa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
item.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. item.title: NLC denies November 30 Jigawa strike over transport allowance
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎The Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, Jigawa State Council, has dismissed reports suggesting that it plans to embark on a strike on November 30, over the alleged failure of the state government to pay workers a N70,000 transport allowance. ‎ ‎In a statement by the State Council’s Secretary, Jide Tanko, the NLC said it was currently in discussions with the Jigawa State Government towards the prompt implementation of the N70,000 transport allowance for workers across the state for an initial six-month period. ‎ ‎The Council described the message circulating on social media as false, urging workers and members of the public to disregard it. ‎ ‎Tanko assured workers that the Council remained committed to ensuring the realisation of the allowance, adding that updates on the negotiations would be communicated through its recognised official channels. ‎ ‎He also cautioned workers against spreading unverified information, emphasising that only communications issued by the recognised NLC leadership and its affiliated unions should be regarded as authentic. ‎ ‎The Jigawa NLC Council thanked workers for their patience, understanding and continued support as engagements with the state government continue. item.title: Nigeria endorses Infantino for another term as FIFA president
item.description: Nigeria has declared its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid to retain the presidency of the world football governing body, FIFA, in the 2027 election. The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s endorsement on Saturday during the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja. Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Dikko said Nigeria would back Infantino’s re-election and called on other African football associations to support his continued leadership. “I must make it clear here on behalf of the Federal Government and in regard to the resolution of all the members of CAF that Nigeria firmly endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the election. “This is a direct message that was given to us by the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. “We recognise Mr Gianni’s contribution to the advancement of football worldwide, particularly in Africa, and urge our fellow African member associations to stand firmly together in support of his continued leadership. “This is in our collective interest,” he added. The NSC chairman also praised Infantino’s administration, drawing on his experience in football management to argue that the FIFA president’s decisions had served the interests of the sport. “Before I conclude, if I put my heart as a football person, Mr President, as a former member of the NFL Exco, Chairman of the League, member of the FIFA Seconders Committee, and founding member of the World League Forum, I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football,” he said. He maintained that Infantino’s central responsibility was to grow the game and generate more revenue, arguing that disagreements within football administration largely concerned how the funds were shared. “His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that. The entire issue we are seeing across the world here today has nothing to do with bringing the revenues or the distribution. It’s all about distributing these revenues,” Dikko said. Nigeria’s declaration came at the same gathering where CAF president Patrice Motsepe reiterated the continental body’s backing for Infantino’s re-election. Infantino, who became FIFA president in 2016, is seeking another four-year term at the election scheduled to hold in Morocco in March 2027 with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima set to challenge him. The post Nigeria endorses Infantino for another term as FIFA president appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil
item.description: A powerful storm with winds exceeding 100 kilometers per hour killed three people and destroyed around 5,000 homes Friday in southern Brazil, as authorities raced to rescue injured survivors and find more casualties in the wreckage. Rain and high winds battered Tupancireta early Friday, tearing up buildings and about 100 trees in the municipality that is home to 20,000 people. “It’s something never seen before, a movie scene,” Tupancireta Mayor Gustavo Herter told local media. “Our hospital was blocked by the trees around it, the access roads to the municipality were blocked with trees. The city is finished,” he said. The hospital’s roof was also destroyed and 11 patients had to be transferred. The city was without electricity and water after the storm hit at around 3 am and lasted less than an hour, Herter said. Three people were found dead, according to the state government of Rio Grande do Sul, where Tupancireta is located. Another 32 municipalities also reported damage. This handout picture released by Rio Grande do Sul Civil Defence Department shows the damage caused by strong winds in Tupancireta, Rio Grande do Sul state, Brazil, on November 20, 2026. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva ordered emergency teams be sent to the region in response to the storm. “We know there was a party in the municipality where the roof of that structure ended up collapsing,” Luciano Boeira, state coordinator of civil defense, told Radio Gaucha. Brazilian meteorologists said winds reached 114 kilometers per hour (70 miles per hour) during the storm. Civil defense described the storm as a “supercell,” which often precedes a tornado with strong upward air currents, and has not ruled out the possibility that a tornado hit the city. State officials have allocated about $330,000 in local currency to respond to the disaster. Southern Brazil is frequently hit by tornadoes. AFP The post Severe Storm Destroys Thousands Of Homes, Kills Three In Brazil appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ‘I’ll be back’: vows Kane after ankle surgery
item.description: Bayern Munich’s star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday. Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern’s 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle. Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d’Or winner had “successfully undergone surgery” on his left ankle. “The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program,” Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months. Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season. “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season.” Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: “tough times don’t last, tough people do”, while thanking his supporters for their messages of support. Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England’s most capped player’s rehabilitation progresses. England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March. The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front. Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday. The post ‘I’ll be back’: vows Kane after ankle surgery appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: We’re not joining your opposition coalition, PDP tells Lukman
item.description: …Snubs November 30 summit, declares Wike’s Rainbow alliance its only coalition By Luminous Jannamike, Abuja The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected claims that it has joined the opposition Coalition for Democracy being promoted by former National Vice Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Salihu Lukman, declaring that it will not attend the coalition’s November 30 summit. The party said it had not entered into any alliance with the coalition, authorised anyone to represent it at the summit or agreed to be bound by any decision taken in its name. It maintained that its only recognised coalition arrangement was the Rainbow Coalition, backed by its National Leader, Nyesom Wike. The position was contained in a statement signed by the PDP National Publicity Secretary, Hon. Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, who said those being presented as the party’s representatives were expelled members with no authority to speak or act on its behalf. Jungudo said the individuals’ claims to the party’s leadership and representation had suffered defeats at the Federal High Court, Court of Appeal and Supreme Court. He added that the courts had issued orders restraining Kabiru Tanimu Turaki, SAN, and his associates from parading themselves as PDP leaders, while imposing financial penalties exceeding N100 million over alleged abuses of court processes and frivolous litigation. Questioning Lukman’s continued engagement with the individuals, Jungudo said, “It is therefore astonishing that Mr Salihu Lukman, who ought to be sufficiently informed about the legal status and recognised leadership of the PDP, would continue to engage these individuals and use them as a basis for associating the party with his so-called Toronto Coalition.” Describing the proposed arrangement as a political project built on misrepresentation, the PDP declared it ‘dead on arrival’, particularly because those being presented as its representatives lacked the authority to speak on its behalf. The party also threatened legal action against Lukman, his associates and other promoters of the Coalition for Democracy if they continued to use its name and institutional identity in their political activities. “The party will not hesitate to pursue appropriate legal action against any person or group that continues to unlawfully associate the PDP with this arrangement,” Jungudo warned. Reiterating its position, the party said the Rainbow Coalition, in line with Wike’s political direction and directives, remained its only recognised coalition arrangement. item.title: Young Protesters Hit Streets Across Europe
item.description: Protesters rallied across Europe on Friday to vent anger over issues from high living costs to military spending and the climate crisis, ramping up pressure on political leaders they accuse of ignoring the concerns of young people. Demonstrators hit the streets in cities from Italy to Germany, Switzerland and Britain, many waving signs emblazoned with “fight for our future”, setting off flares and burning cardboard models of tanks. The rallies, coordinated by a youth-led coalition of over 50 groups, are fuelled by grievances that vary from place to place, including Israel’s war in Gaza, high rents and deteriorating learning conditions at schools and universities. But a common theme runs through them — a sense that governments across the continent are too busy with geopolitical crises and helping big business, and not investing enough in the well-being of younger generations. Olivia Ferrario, an 18-year-old high school student at a protest in the Italian city of Milan, told AFP that young people were displaying their “dynamism and determination” by taking to the streets. “If the government does not listen to us, we cannot remain silent,” she said at the demonstration that attracted tens of thousands of protesters. Police deployed in large numbers due to fears of a repeat of the street violence that has marred recent major protests in France and other countries. Protesters dressed up as clowns jump during a youth demonstration under the motto “Stop ReArm Europe!” ‘Lost So Much Hope’ In Switzerland, organisers claimed that more than 40,000 protesters had taken to the streets nationwide. “Austerity is social violence,” read a banner in Lausanne, while another blared: “Be vegan, but eat the rich.” The demonstrations were mostly peaceful. But a small number of people clashed with police after it ended, resulting in the deployment of tear gas and water cannon, the domestic Keystone-ATS news agency reported. In Berlin, about 1,000 university students and school pupils protested over concerns including Germany’s rapid rearmament, which has stoked fears of a return to compulsory military service. “I simply think it’s indefensible… to force someone to learn how to fight and kill, and then send them to war,” Helena Kossatz, 18, who finished high school last year, told AFP. While Europe seeks to rearm in the face of a hostile Russia, organisers of the continent-wide protests say funds allocated to rearmament should be spent on education, youth policies and housing. Several hundred protesters, some in school uniform, gathered at demonstrations in London outside parliament and in nearby Trafalgar Square, waving placards that said “save higher education” and “Fight for our futures not their wars”. “I’ve lost so much hope,” Eliz, who had taken the day off from college and gave only one name, told AFP. item.title: 10th anniversary: Oba Ewuare II’s reign strengthens traditional institution — Sultan
item.description: The Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has congratulated the Oba of Benin, Oba Ewuare II, on his 10th coronation anniversary, commending his leadership and commitment to cultural preservation, peacebuilding and national unity. The Sultan described the anniversary as a significant milestone marking a decade of traditional leadership and dedication to the progress and well-being of the Benin Kingdom and its people. In a statement issued on Saturday by Prince Bashir Adefaka, for the Sultan’s Media Team, Abubakar praised the monarch for upholding the cultural heritage, traditions and historical identity of the Benin Kingdom. He also commended Oba Ewuare II for promoting peaceful coexistence, mutual respect and unity among Nigerians across ethnic, religious and cultural divides. The Sultan noted that traditional institutions remained indispensable to national cohesion, the promotion of moral values, community development and peaceful coexistence, particularly at a time when Nigeria needed the collective wisdom and leadership of traditional rulers to address its challenges. He said the Oba’s 10-year reign had reinforced the importance of traditional institutions as custodians of history, culture, values and the aspirations of their people. According to him, the Benin monarch has also continued to serve as a rallying point for unity, stability and development. Abubakar, who is physically present in Benin City for the anniversary celebration, expressed delight at being part of the historic occasion. He said his presence demonstrated the enduring bonds of brotherhood, friendship and mutual respect among traditional rulers in Nigeria, irrespective of ethnic and regional differences. The Sultan prayed for continued good health, wisdom, strength and long life for Oba Ewuare II, urging divine guidance for the monarch as he leads the Benin Kingdom towards greater peace, prosperity and development. He also prayed for sustained peace and progress in the Benin Kingdom, Edo State and Nigeria. item.title: Sultan arrives Benin to honour Oba Ewuare II on 10th coronation anniversary
item.description: The Sultan of Sokoto, His Eminence Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar, has arrived Benin City, Edo State, ahead of the 10th coronation anniversary of the Oba of Benin, Omo N’Oba N’Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II, Oba of Benin. The aircraft conveying the Sultan touched ground at the Oba Akenzua II Airport in the Edo State capital 25 minutes after departing the Samuel Ladoke Akintola International Airport, Ibadan, Oyo State, at 5:05 p.m. on Friday, November 20. In a statement by Prince Bashir Adefaka on behalf of the Media Team of the Sultan of Sokoto, noted that the Sultan was received by senior members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council at the airport. He was accompanied on the flight by the Galadiman Gerin Sokoto, His Royal Highness Alhaji Aliyu Attahiru Galadanci, and former Director-General, National Broadcasting Commission, NBC, Mallam Danladi Bako, Kogunan Sokoto. The Sultan arrived Ibadan on a weeklong South-West working visit on Sunday, November 15, starting off his activities with participation in the 11th General Assembly of the Muslim Ummah of South West Nigeria, MUSWEN, as special guest of honour. The Sultan also performed his duty as Chancellor of the University of Ibadan on Tuesday, November 17, supported by his Pro-Chancellor and Chairman Governing Council, Chief Bisi Akande, as well as the new Vice-Chancellor, Professor Peter Olamakinde Olapegba, among others. On Wednesday, he travelled from his Ibadan to Saki to partake – as Chairman of the Day – in the official commissioning of the 500-seat Alhaji Azeez Adedokun Olowolagba Information and Communication Technology, ICT, Centre built and donated to the College of Nursing Sciences, Muslim Medical Foundation Saki, by Alhaji Mudasiru Adedokun Olowolagba, in memory of his late father. On Thursday, the Sultan paid a courtesy call on the Aseyin of Iseyin, Oba Sefiu Olawale Adeyemi III (Ajirotutu I), who will be celebrating his third coronation anniversary on December 11. He also witnessed the award ceremony by the Iseyin Kingdom in honour of legal luminary and philanthropist, Barrister Ahmed Raji (SAN). On Friday, the Sultan of Sokoto paid a courtesy visit to the palace of the Olubadan of Ibadan Land, where Oba Rashidi Ladoja, Arusa I, assisted by Olubadan-in-Council, received him. Both monarchs then proceeded to the Bodija Muslim Community Central Mosque, Ibadan, where they observed their Jumat service led by the Chief Imam, Sheikh Hakeem Ibrahim. He the left for Benin City, where he was first received by members of the Oba of Benin-in-Council and then later by the royal host himself in his palace the same Friday night. item.title: Countries race to secure COP31 deal after fossil fuel row
item.description: The COP31 climate talks spilled into Saturday as countries raced to secure a deal after a draft text dropped all mention of fossil fuels, exposing deep divisions over how to tackle global warming. Nearly 200 nations remained deadlocked after two weeks of grinding UN talks in Turkey, with negotiators working through the night after missing their scheduled Friday finish amid feuds over energy, science and finance. Australia, which is presiding over the COP31 negotiations, raced against the clock to produce a third draft deal, with many delegates due to catch flights home. “We are close to the finish line, but we are not there yet,” COP31 President Murat Kurum, who is Turkey’s environment minister, told an assembly late Friday that approved some technical matters. Midway through his opening address, Kurum was forced to pause while a protester shouted “You are killing the future!” before being escorted from the hall. Expectations of a major breakthrough have been low at COP31 as countries grapple with an oil price shock and geopolitical tensions stemming from the war in Iran. The summit follows a string of climate-linked disasters from Europe to Nepal and Indonesia and unfolds as a super El Nino pattern amplifies the risk of further extreme weather. A draft deal unveiled earlier this week called for a faster phase-out of fossil fuels, a flashpoint at UN climate talks where producers such as Saudi Arabia have fiercely resisted such calls. A second, pared-down draft released on Thursday stripped away all mentions of fossil fuels — sending negotiators rushing back to the bargaining table. The European Union said the revised draft “risks turning this climate COP into a fossil summit”. A dozen European and developing countries — from France to Panama and the Solomon Islands — released a letter Friday insisting that the deal include “a clear transition away from fossil fuels”. Panama, which also signed the letter, threatened to walk away from the talks. The country’s environment minister, Juan Carlos Navarro, is a vocal critic of the climate negotiations, accusing a “petroleum mafia” of blocking progress. Meanwhile, the OPEC oil cartel wrote on X that its head, Haitham Al Ghais, met Russian presidential climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at COP31 to discuss “the importance of inclusive and balanced approaches across all multilateral environmental fora”. – ‘Clean electrification’ – Australia’s Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who shuttled between delegations to seek compromises, said Friday he would work “for as long as it takes, to get the job done”. The draft “cover decision” proposes a target to electrify the global economy — a push to replace technologies that burn fossil fuels directly, like diesel cars and gas heating, with electric alternatives. item.title: 2027: INEC REC seeks traditional rulers’ support for peaceful, secure elections in Benue
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, has called on traditional rulers in the state to promote a peaceful and secure environment before and during the 2027 general elections. Idris made the appeal during a courtesy visit to the Tor Tiv and Chairman of the Benue State Council of Traditional Rulers, His Royal Majesty, Orcivirigh Prof. James Ayatse, on Friday, November 20, 2026, as part of the Commission’s stakeholder engagement ahead of the elections. The REC also solicited the support of the traditional institution in encouraging eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and strengthening collaboration with INEC to ensure successful conduct of the forthcoming polls. According to a statement by the Public Affairs Officer of INEC in Benue State, Mrs. Peace Ogoyi, Idris described the visit as a vital step in the Commission’s preparations for the 2027 elections. “He solicited the intervention and support of the royal father in three key areas: encouraging the collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), promoting a peaceful and secure environment before and during the elections, and providing further support to the Commission through sustained collaboration.” Responding, the Tor Tiv welcomed the REC and his delegation, expressing appreciation for the visit and acknowledging the important role of traditional rulers in ensuring a conducive environment for electoral activities. He noted that “traditional rulers, as fathers of the state, have a responsibility to receive electoral officials and ensure their safety and provision of a peaceful working environment. Drawing from his experience in previous elections, including his service in various ad hoc capacities and as a State Returning Officer, Ayatse acknowledged the enormous responsibilities confronting the Commission. He said the Traditional Council had consistently advocated peaceful political campaigns and a level playing field for all political parties. The monarch further disclosed that traditional and religious leaders had organised prayers for peaceful elections and maintained constructive engagements with security agencies to strengthen peace and security across the state. He assured the REC that the Council would continue to collaborate with relevant stakeholders to identify and address electoral security flashpoints ahead of the elections. On the credibility of the electoral process, the Tor Tiv emphasised the need for INEC to uphold the will of the people, urging the Commission’s personnel to discharge their duties with neutrality, fairness and professionalism.
